note: Levels where big players act. Four families: where they showed their hand (intervention, options, positioning, flow, floors); their cost basis (anchored VWAP, volume profile); the reference points they hedge and report against (year / quarter opens, prior-quarter range); and macro forced-hand levels (rate-spread fair value, exporter pain, bond yield caps, fixing bands and pegs).

intervention.desc: Central bank / finance ministry stepped in or warned here

options.desc: Large option strike or barrier being defended

flow.desc: Heavy institutional buying or selling reaction

cb-floor.desc: Stated or implied central-bank floor or cap

avwap.desc: Anchored VWAP from a key day (central-bank decision, intervention, big data surprise). Price above = institutions positioned since then are in profit; below = under water.

volume-profile.desc: High-volume node, point of control or value-area edge: where the big business got done. Acceptance or rejection there matters.

period-open.desc: Year or quarter open, prior-quarter high or low. Funds and banks hedge and report against these.

rate-spread.desc: Fair value implied by the 2Y yield gap. Price stretched far from it = price and rates disagree (the pricing gap).

exporter-pain.desc: Exchange rate companies say they can live with (e.g. Tankan large manufacturers' assumed USD/JPY). Beyond it, pressure builds on the central bank.

yield-cap.desc: Bond yield where a central bank has stepped in before or caps it (BoJ 10Y cap under YCC, BoE gilt buying 2022).

fixing-peg.desc: Official fix, band or peg (PBoC daily CNY fix and its ±2% band, SNB EUR/CHF 1.20 floor 2011-2015).

statuses.historical: No longer active; kept as context
